standfirst: This issue covers ChatGPT moving deeper into business software, Codex case studies from legal and other teams, and skills you can try this week.
digest: OpenAI and Oracle are widening their partnership to bring Oracle's business apps and agents into ChatGPT, and Uber is rolling ChatGPT Work out to more than 30,000 staff. Anthropic also announced a 40% discount on Claude for government partners through GSA, and Claude Code 2.1.312 is out.

Codex case studies dominate the video list. Shopify's CTO, HashiCorp's Mitchell Hashimoto and Sotira each show a different way to use it, including one speaker who says not being technical is no reason not to build. They are easy to borrow when a client asks what people actually do with agents.

For legal and professional services clients, the AT&T and Cooley clips share one message: AI does the groundwork and people stay responsible for the answer. Matt Wolfe also tests Google's new Gemini 4 Argon with five prompts, a quick way to see what it can do.

Anthropic donated the Agent Skills standard to the Agentic AI Foundation, and more than 70 platforms already support it. The tools this week are mostly skills and desktop apps: Hallmark and Impeccable for design, Claude SEO for audits, Call.md for meetings.
One caution: a Claude Code user reports service errors using up their paid limits. It is a single account, but worth knowing if your team relies on Claude Code every day.

items.title: AT&T's legal team uses AI while lawyers keep the decisions
items.summary: AT&T's David McAtee and Bill Ryan explain how AI can support legal work while lawyers keep strategy and judgment. A short framing for cautious clients.

items.title: Mitchell Hashimoto ends his day by putting Codex agents to work
items.summary: Agents research competitors, compare tools and prototype half-formed features before the next morning. A routine any consultant could copy with an AI assistant.

items.title: Shopify's CTO brings a Codex prototype to the meeting
items.summary: Mikhail Parakhin uses Codex to delegate tasks and explore architecture options, so ideas arrive as prototypes. Shows how prototype-first conversations can work.

items.title: Sotira uses Codex to give unsold inventory a second life
items.summary: Amrita Bhasin says being non-technical is no reason not to build, and uses Codex to connect unsold products with buyers. Good for sceptical clients.

items.title: Cooley speeds up IPO preparation with a tool built on OpenAI
items.summary: Cooley's GO Public puts substantive work in front of clients sooner and flags issues earlier, with people still reviewing every answer. Relevant to professional services.

items.title: Higgsfield stretches AI video from one minute to over ten
items.summary: Credits GPT-6 Astra for longer videos and GPT-Image-2.5 for readable text in infographics. Worth a look if clients ask what AI video can do now.

items.title: Matt Wolfe tests five prompts on Google's Gemini 4 Argon
items.summary: A short clip trying five different uses of Google's new Gemini 4 Argon model. Quick way to see what it handles before a client asks.

items.title: Claude Code 2.1.312 adds Entra ID identity option for gateway
items.summary: Admins can pick which sign-in claim identifies users, and fullscreen users can click a queued message to send it now. Mostly matters for enterprise rollouts.

items.title: Oracle's business apps and AI agents are coming to ChatGPT
items.summary: Matters for clients on Oracle software, who may reach those apps from ChatGPT. The partnership also powers new Oracle offerings.

items.title: Anthropic offers government partners 40% off Claude through GSA
items.summary: A new GSA agreement discounts Claude Enterprise, Claude for Government and the API by 40%. A useful reference for public-sector pricing conversations.

items.title: Anthropic donates Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation
items.summary: More than 70 platforms, including ChatGPT, Cursor and GitHub Copilot, already support skills. It means a skill you build should work across tools.

items.title: Uber rolls out ChatGPT Work to 30,000 employees
items.summary: Staff will use it for research, data analysis, presentations and multi-step workflows. A scale reference for clients weighing a company-wide rollout.

sections.title: Tools and skills you can use

items.title: Hallmark is an anti-AI-slop design skill for coding agents
items.summary: Works with Claude Code, Cursor and Codex to keep generated designs from looking generic. Install it into your agent to try.

items.title: Impeccable gives your coding agent a design vocabulary
items.summary: Commands like polish, bolder, critique and audit let you steer and review designs, and catch generic AI output before it ships. Needs a coding agent.

items.title: Claude SEO adds 26 sub-skills for SEO audits in Claude Code
items.summary: Covers technical SEO, schema, local and e-commerce SEO, and PDF or Excel reports. Useful for web clients; optional extensions add live data.

items.title: Call.md records and analyses meetings with real-time AI
items.summary: Gives agents live context from calls, from prep to follow-up. Test on an internal call first; setup effort is not stated.

items.title: VoiceStudio runs voice cloning and dubbing fully on your own machine
items.summary: Open-source tool covering transcription, dictation, video dubbing and audiobooks in 646 languages. Handy for client content, though voice cloning needs consent.

items.title: Openbot runs persistent AI teammates in a local desktop app
items.summary: Runs Codex, Claude and Grok with their own workspaces, task queues and browser control, all in a local-first desktop app.

items.title: Claude-mem carries context from one agent session to the next
items.summary: Captures what your agent does, compresses it with AI and feeds relevant parts back into later sessions. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and Copilot.

items.title: Claude Code builds a pizzeria its own ordering app
items.summary: Aims to spare restaurants the 25 to 30% delivery-app fee, with Claude Code writing the app and backend. A real build with a paying customer.

items.title: Anthropic reports early progress on drug development with Claude
items.summary: Anthropic's own update on using Claude to speed up drug development, with a busy Hacker News discussion. Useful background for life sciences clients.

items.title: Claude Code user reports usage spike and drained paid limits
items.summary: A Pro subscriber says service errors drained their five-hour allowance and Anthropic will not compensate. One user's account, but useful if your team hits limits.
